tagline: Enhancing corporate value by deepening society's trust in the firm and increasing the satisfaction of stakeholders.
hero_kpi_rationale: Net revenue is the primary indicator of Nomura's overall financial performance, reflecting growth across its three key divisions (Wealth Management, Investment Management, and Wholesale).

kpis.name: Net Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated by the company after deducting direct costs.
kpis.description: Net revenue increased by 21.2% for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, demonstrating notable expansion of the company's operations.
kpis.signal: Significant net revenue growth, indicating strong operational performance.

kpis.name: Wealth Management Division Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by wealth management services.
kpis.description: The Wealth Management division saw its revenue increase by 12.2% for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, driven by increased flows and assets under management.
kpis.signal: Solid wealth management revenue growth, driven by comprehensive services.

kpis.name: Investment Management Division Revenue
kpis.description: The Investment Management division recorded a 24.9% increase in revenue for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, benefiting from increased assets under management.
kpis.signal: Strong investment management revenue growth, reaching record levels.

kpis.name: Wholesale Division Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by wholesale activities, including global markets and investment banking.
kpis.description: The Wholesale division saw its revenue increase by 22.1% for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, driven by strong performance in global markets and investment banking.
kpis.signal: Robust Wholesale division revenue growth, supported by all business lines.

kpis.name: Diluted Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Share of net income attributable to each outstanding common share.
kpis.description: Diluted earnings per share more than doubled, increasing from JPY 52.69 to JPY 111.03 for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025.
kpis.signal: Earnings per share doubled, indicating significant improvement in per-share profitability.

kpis.name: Return on Equity
kpis.explanation: Measures the company's profitability relative to shareholders' equity.
kpis.description: Return on equity reached 10.0% for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, in line with long-term management targets.
kpis.signal: ROE target achieved, indicating effective capital management.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Amount of dividend paid per common share.
kpis.description: A total dividend of JPY 57 per share will be paid for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, comprising an ordinary dividend of JPY 24 and a commemorative dividend of JPY 10.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in total dividend, including a commemorative dividend.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.238 last year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $112.541 billion last year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 33.0% last year.

kpis.name: Wealth Management Income Before Taxes
kpis.explanation: Wealth Management division profit before tax deduction.
kpis.description: The Wealth Management division recorded income before taxes of JPY 170.8 billion for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, the highest in 11 years, driven by a stable growth strategy.
kpis.signal: Wealth Management division income before taxes reaches 11-year high.

kpis.name: Alternative Assets Under Management
kpis.explanation: Value of alternative assets managed by the company.
kpis.description: Alternative assets under management increased by 40.2% to reach JPY 2,608.2 billion as of March 31, 2025, underscoring the success of the expansion strategy in this area.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in alternative assets under management, indicating increased demand for these asset classes.

kpis.name: Investment Banking Income Before Taxes
kpis.explanation: Investment Banking division profit before tax deduction.
kpis.description: The Investment Banking division saw its income before taxes increase by 208.4% to reach JPY 166.3 billion as of March 31, 2025, driven by high client activity and service expansion.
kpis.signal: Spectacular growth in investment banking income before taxes, reaching record levels.

kpis.name: Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares outstanding during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate earnings per share: basis for calculating the Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Intense competition from non-traditional financial firms and FinTech
risks.summary: Nomura faces growing competition not only from large universal banks and broker-dealers, but also from online platforms, FinTech companies, and non-financial enterprises digitalizing financial services. Industry consolidation (bank-insurance-emerging player alliances) strengthens competitors capable of offering integrated services that Nomura cannot always match.
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned in section 2 (high rank in index), strong language: 'intensely competitive,' 'increasingly fierce competitive environment,' 'may lose business or transactions.' Upward trend with rise of FinTech and entry of non-financial players. Competition category is central for a global broker-dealer.

risks.title: Forced revision of Nomura's international business model
risks.summary: Nomura acknowledges the need to continually revise its global business model to remain competitive in US, European, and Asian markets. Acquisitions (e.g., Greentech Capital in 2020) and divestitures (e.g., Capital Nomura Securities in 2023) illustrate this strategic instability, with risk of costs exceeding forecasts and unrealized synergies.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in subsection 2(3), with high uncertainty language: 'may require further revision,' 'assumptions may not be accurate,' 'could even harm our business.' Stable but persistent trend across multiple strategic cycles. High weight as it impacts the group's overall profitability.

risks.title: Regulatory risk and compliance across multiple jurisdictions
risks.summary: Nomura operates under extensive and evolving regulations in numerous countries (Japan, United States, Europe, Asia), including anti-money laundering rules, capital requirements, and trading activity constraints. Failures can result in heavy fines, activity restrictions, or reputational damage, as illustrated by the explicit mention of AML/CTF risks (section 19(5)).
risks.score_rationale: Section 19 covers five distinct regulatory sub-risks, positioned at the top of operational/legal risks. Imperative language: 'extensive regulation limits our activities,' 'significant penalties and losses,' 'tightening of regulations.' Upward trend with post-crisis tightening. Critical category for a global player subject to FSA, SEC, and FCA simultaneously.

risks.title: Cybersecurity, system outages, and confidential information leaks
risks.summary: Nomura is exposed to risks of cyberattacks, IT failures, and data leaks that could disrupt its trading, asset management, and investment banking operations. The growing cost of maintaining adequate cybersecurity also puts pressure on margins, in a context where critical financial infrastructure is a priority target.
risks.score_rationale: Dedicated section 21, with direct reference to 'system failure, information leakage and cost of maintaining sufficient cybersecurity.' Explicit language on financial and operational impact. Upward trend in the global financial sector. Nomura also cites operational resilience as a key issue in section 3.

risks.title: Unauthorized disclosure of client personal data
risks.summary: Nomura holds significant volumes of client personal data in its Wealth Management and asset management activities. Unauthorized disclosure or misuse of this data could result in regulatory sanctions (notably under Japanese data protection laws and equivalent foreign regulations) and damage client trust.
risks.score_rationale: Section 20 specifically dedicated to personal data protection, distinct from general cybersecurity. Moderate but precise language: 'unauthorized disclosure or misuse of personal information.' Stable trend with strengthening GDPR/APPI regulations. Medium weight but significant reputational and legal impact.

risks.title: Reputational risk related to conflicts of interest and employee conduct
risks.summary: As an integrated group combining investment banking, proprietary trading, and asset management, Nomura is structurally exposed to conflicts of interest between its various business lines. Acts of fraud, malfeasance, or poor management of these conflicts by employees or executives could severely damage its reputation and client relationships, with lasting commercial consequences.
risks.score_rationale: Sections 15, 17, and 18 jointly address reputation, internal fraud, and conflicts of interest. Strong language: 'misconduct, fraud or other criminal activity,' 'relationships with clients could be harmed,' 'failure to identify conflicts of interest.' Stable trend but structural risk for an integrated player (investment banking + asset management). History of sector scandals reinforces severity.

risks.title: Inability to recruit and retain key talent in a competitive market
risks.summary: Nomura depends on highly qualified professionals (bankers, traders, managers) in a highly competitive global talent market. Repeated restructurings and compensation reductions related to strategic revisions risk weakening the group's ability to attract and retain the profiles needed for its development, particularly in its international markets.
risks.score_rationale: Dedicated section 22, with additional mention in section 2(3) on the risk of workforce reduction as part of strategic restructuring. Direct language: 'unable to hire, retain and develop qualified personnel.' Upward trend in a global financial talent market under strain. Risk amplified by Nomura's recurring restructurings.

risks.title: Sustainability risks and exposure to ESG and climate criticism
risks.summary: Nomura is exposed to climate change-related risks (physical risks to its assets and operations) and the transition to a low-carbon economy (transition risks affecting its clients and portfolios). Insufficient communication on ESG issues or an inability to support clients in their transition could harm its reputation and regulatory compliance in jurisdictions strengthening sustainability requirements.
risks.score_rationale: Section 4 entirely dedicated, with distinction between physical risk and transition risk. Evolving language: 'rapidly changing circumstances around sustainability,' 'deemed a lack of sufficient focus,' 'unable to adequately respond to strengthening of regulations.' Upward trend with multiplication of ESG reporting obligations. New but growing risk for Japanese financial institutions.

ai_positioning.summary: Nomura Holdings integrates AI solutions into its financial services to improve efficiency and client value. The company emphasizes AI for wealth management and investment services.
evidence: Management strategy aims to increase shareholder value by improving productivity and expanding revenue sources.
The Wealth Management division is strengthening its services using digital tools and AI solutions to meet client needs.
The Investment Management division is developing internal active investment capabilities and private asset management services.
